[[File:Ronaldo in 2018.jpg|thumb|[[Cristiano Ronaldo]] is the competition's all-time top scorer with 140 goals]]
The [[UEFA Champions League]], known until 1992 as the European Champion Clubs' Cup or colloquially as the European Cup, is an annual [[association football]] cup competition organised by [[UEFA]] since 1955. Originally a straight knockout competition open only to champion clubs, the tournament was expanded during the 1990s to incorporate a round-robin group phase and more teams. The expansion resulted in more games being played, increasing players' goalscoring chances; thus the rankings are weighted in favour of modern players: only five out of the 50 players on the list never competed in the reformed Champions League.

With 140 goals, [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] is currently the all-time top scorer in the Champions League, with [[Lionel Messi]] and [[Robert Lewandowski]] being the only other players to have reached triple figures. Ronaldo has also finished as the top scorer [[List of UEFA Champions League top scorers#By player|for the most individual seasons]] in the competition's history, doing so seven times.

The title of highest goalscorer had previously been held by [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]], who scored his 50th goal in 2005 while at [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] to overtake [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://as.com/futbol/2005/09/28/mas_futbol/1127858431_850215.html |title=Raúl ya es el máximo goleador de la Copa de Europa |trans-title=Raúl is now the top scorer of the European Cup |date=28 September 2005 |access-date=25 October 2023 |work=[[Diario AS]] |location=[[Madrid]], Spain |language=es}}</ref> He held the record until November 2014,<ref>{{cite web |last=Hunter |first=Graham |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/37393011/cristiano-ronaldo-track-break |title=Look out, Messi, Ronaldo is the real record breaker |date=30 May 2014 |access-date=25 October 2023 |work=[[ESPN]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Bate |first=Adam |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11946/9527119/lionel-messi-and-cristiano-ronaldo-are-closing-in-on-rauls-uefa-champions-league-goalscoring-record-of-71 |title=Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo are closing in on Raul's UEFA Champions League goalscoring record of 71 |date=2 November 2014 |access-date=25 October 2023 |work=[[Sky Sports]]}}</ref> when his eventual tally of 71 was first equalled and then surpassed by Messi.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Arnett |first1=George |last2=Sedghi |first2=Ami |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/datablog/2014/nov/07/champions-league-goalscoring-record-charting-messi-ronaldo-and-raul |title=Champions League goalscoring record: charting Messi, Ronaldo and Raúl |date=7 November 2014 |access-date=25 October 2023 |work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/29363780 |title=Messi breaks Champions League record |date=25 November 2014 |access-date=25 October 2023 |work=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref> Ronaldo has remained the competition's outright top scorer since September 2015; after a back-and-forth exchange of the record between him and Messi, a hat-trick by the former against [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]] put Ronaldo ahead with 80 goals, and he would not relinquish the top spot again after this.<ref>{{cite news |date=15 September 2015 |title=Ronaldo reaches 80 goals as Madrid fell Shakhtar |work=[[UEFA]] |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0225-0e91a963c678-dee34c931cf8-1000--ronaldo-reaches-80-goals-as-madrid-fell-shakhtar/ |access-date=25 October 2023}}</ref>
